reuse.why: It reuses getRangeAmount and getApproxNumberThreshold and collapses five inline null/number/range ternaries, but adds getPlannedAmount next to the existing getScheduledAmount (same null/number/range dispatch) instead of extending that one.

duplication.why: getPlannedAmount re-implements getScheduledAmount's null-to-0 / number / getRangeAmount dispatch, so two shared amount functions now coexist; the server-side inline copies are removed though.

placement.why: The new rule is placed correctly in shared/schedules.ts and server callers delegate to it.

scope.why: Only the amount call sites, the new helper, the forecast input type and tests are touched.

maintainability.why: Two near-identical exported amount functions with diverging behaviour (only one knows about isapprox) invite future drift and confusion about which to call.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts getPlannedAmount is added alongside the existing getScheduledAmount instead of extending it; getScheduledAmount callers (api-models expectedAmount, Balance.tsx, SchedulesTable, mobile schedules, useScheduleEdit) keep the old rule.

disguised_duplication.where: getPlannedAmount in shared/schedules.ts reorders getScheduledAmount's null/number/range checks (range tested first via typeof !== 'number') under a new name.

one_place.where: The approximate rule lives in getPlannedAmount (server posting, actions, forecast, preview, schedule-template), but getScheduledAmount, used by the API expectedAmount and UI balances/lists, still plans approximate amounts at their exact value.
